The prevalence of these lineages peaked at 75.7% (95% CI = 73.8%–77.5%) for BA.1.1 by the week ending February 19, 2022
the fastest doubling times were observed for XBB.1.16 (15.7 days; 95% CI = 13.9–17.9)
The number of cases attributed to each lineage was highest for BA.1.1 (14 million), B.1.1.529 (9.8 million) and BA.5 (8.0 million)
reaching a peak prevalence of 84.1% (95% CI = 81.4%–86.5%) by April 1
The fastest doubling times among lineages assessed at 1% prevalence during January 2, 2022–May 13, 2023, occurred for BA.2.12.1 (5.4 days; 95% CI = 4.8–6.1)

ev.q: All methods included weighting to account for the complex survey design and adjust for potential sampling biases.
Each submitting laboratory source was considered a primary sampling unit, and the state and week of sequence sample collection were considered strata.

procedures.name: multinomial regression nowcast
procedures.inferred_from: 'multinomial regression' → logistic family (multinomial); used for nowcast proportions of most recent weeks and for growth rates/doubling times

ev.q: nowcasts were generated using multinomial regression fit on the previous 21 weeks of data.
Doubling times for proportions of specific lineages are based on instantaneous growth rates from the multinomial nowcasting model.
BA.5, XBB.1.5, and BA.1.1 remained predominant for the longest durations (19, 16, and 10 weeks, respectively).
